author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating to human: public-API breaking change on DownloadBlobParams.expected_sha256 (Option<&str> → Option<&Sha256>). Same scope-of-decision as JMAP-6r7c.50: 0.1.1 jmap-base-client crate, workspace AGENTS.md says 'Prefer non-breaking changes. Reshape only when the workspace is bumping a major.'

The reshape is sound on its own merits — eliminates is_valid_sha256_hex helper, the InvalidArgument("expected_sha256 is not 64-char hex") branch, and the to_ascii_lowercase normalize, replacing them all with the typed Sha256 wrapper's deserialize-time ABNF guarantee. This is exactly the parse-don't-validate posture this crate already adopted for BlobUploadResponse.sha256 in bd:JMAP-v9py.13.

Recommendation: bundle with JMAP-6r7c.50 (UploadBlobParams reshape) and JMAP-6r7c.20 (AuthProvider::auth_header secret-typing) into a single 0.2.0 minor-bump epic. All three are 'pay the SemVer cost once and ratify the type-design discipline' changes; landing them together amortises the version bump and the per-consumer migration effort.

Same caveats as JMAP-6r7c.50: no current workspace consumer calls download_blob with an external String (the test sites are all in this crate). Ripple to jmap-mail-client / jmap-chat-client is zero today.
